items.author: joeywan-google
items.summary: The PD mini load balancer's returns 200 without contacting any server. A health check on the LB therefore stays green while every prefill and decode engine is down.
items.body:
## Motivation

The PD mini load balancer's `/health` returns 200 without contacting any server. A health check on the LB therefore stays green while every prefill and decode engine is down. `/health_generate` is also blind. It returns 200 when an engine answers 503, and a bare 500 when an engine refuses the connection.

items.summary: The torch indexer of DeepSeek-V4.1 (the path GPUs without DeepGEMM's paged MQA logits take, e.g. SM12x) scores a prefill in chunks of a bf16 product capped at (1 GiB).
items.body:
## Motivation

The torch indexer of DeepSeek-V4.1 (the path GPUs without DeepGEMM's paged MQA logits take, e.g. SM12x) scores a prefill in chunks of a bf16 `[rows, 64 heads, keys]` product capped at `_TORCH_SCORE_BUDGET_BYTES` (1 GiB). `scores()` then did `(s.relu() * weights.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1)`: `relu()` and the multiply each allocated another tensor of the chunk's size, so a chunk peaked at 3 GiB. On 12-16 GB cards that is the largest transient of a long prefill, and it is where the prefill runs out of memory.

items.author: nbommi19
items.summary: The chunk planner still budgets each chunk as. This PR budgets CUDA chunks as, which matches the buffer that is actually allocated. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Since #61149, DeepGEMM returns the CUDA sparse-indexer prefill logits as `[rows, max_seqlen_k]`, where `max_seqlen_k` is the longest key range in the chunk. The chunk planner (`_split_indexer_prefill_chunks`) still budgets each chunk as `rows x total keys of all requests`. This PR budgets CUDA chunks as `rows x longest request`, which matches the buffer that is actually allocated.

items.author: fangyuchu

## Overview


#61767 introduced `cpu_all_reduce_` (`vllm/distributed/utils.py`), a low-latency gloo all-reduce for the DP hot path — `ParallelConfig.sync_dp_state` (engine-side DP state sync) and `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding` (worker-side DP padding/cudagraph coordination). It replaced `torch.distributed.all_reduce` with raw `group.send`/`group.recv` p2p ops waited on via bare `work.wait()`.

A bare `wait()` never times out: the gloo group's default timeout is not applied to these p2p waits. So since #61767, `--cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds` silently no longer takes effect on the DP sync

items.author: WhatGhost
items.summary: On wave64 (MI300/MI355), with N=5 picks YTILE 3/4 for wide M. These tiles exceed the VGPR budget and spill, so a 5-row BF16 GEMM is ~4x slower than a 4-row one. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

On wave64 (MI300/MI355), `wvSplitK` with N=5 picks YTILE 3/4 for wide M. These tiles exceed the VGPR budget and spill, so a 5-row BF16 GEMM is ~4x slower than a 4-row one. This PR keeps N=5 at YTILE 2 on wave64.

## Claims

- 5-row BF16 GEMM on wide M is ~4x faster on MI355X (e.g. 32B lm_head 930 → 235 us).
- Speculative decoding with 5 rows per verify step (conc=1, `num_speculative_tokens=4`) gets 2.07x output throughput (Qwen3.8-27B MTP).
- No change for other N or for wave32 (gfx11/gfx12).

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), same build. Only `_rocm_C.abi3.so` is swapped between

`--tool-call-parser kimi_k3` emits nothing while the model generates a tool call. `parse_streaming_increment()` matched only a **complete** call through `_CALL_RE`, so not even the tool name shipped until `<|close|>call<|sep|>` arrived — and the whole argument blob was then delivered as a single delta. items.body:
# MegaMoE Support Status and Roadmap
This Roadmap is based on the [dev branch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/tree/dev)

## Summary

Adds an opt-in `token_order: morton` knob to `SolAttentionConfig`. Sol-Attn routes per 64-token block over the flattened video sequence; in Wan's native T-H-W raster order a block is a run along width (on the 720p grid a 64-token block spans 73 tokens along W and 1 row along H), so routing decisions have weak 3D locality. items.title: [Fix] sgl-router: Do not abort forwarded requests on reqwest's default 30 s TCP_USER_TIMEOUT
items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: Disables reqwest's default 30s TCP_USER_TIMEOUT on Linux so the router no longer aborts forwarded requests when engines briefly stall reading request bodies.
items.body:
## Motivation

The router's forwarding client is a default `reqwest` 0.12 client. On Linux, `reqwest` sets `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT` to 30 s on every connection unless told otherwise (`reqwest-0.12.28/src/async_impl/client.rs:307`). If an engine reads none of a forwarded request's body for 30 s, the kernel aborts the router's send with `ETIMEDOUT`. That can happen when the engine's HTTP process is busy with a burst of long prompts and stops reading request bodies. The router then answers 504 `upstream_timeout` after about 30.5 s, regardless of `request_timeout`.

We hit this in agentic trace replays:

items.body:
### Summary

Occasionally a long-context request ends **mid-sentence**, and on the server side it looks like a perfectly normal completion: `finish_reason="stop"`, `stop_reason=null`, no abort/error counters. With `return_token_ids: true` the final token is `248046` (`<|im_end|>`), i.e. the model itself ended the turn. Clients just see a truncated answer with no error, which is very confusing for an agent workload.

I would like to understand whether this is expected behaviour at very long context, and which knob (if any) reduces it. Happy to run any A/B you suggest.

### Environment

- 2x RTX

`Glm4MoeMultiTokenPredictorLayer.forward` returns the residual sum *before* the final `shared_head.norm`. As a

items.title: Batch-invariant ordered TP reductions for TP>=3
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: For a given element, NCCL's summation order depends on where that element sits in the message (ring rotation, chunking, and the algorithm it picks for the message size). The training forward ( rows) and the inference engine (flat decode rows) place the same to…
items.body:
## Problem

Under `batch_invariant_mode`, tensor-parallel forward reductions at TP >= 3 are not batch-invariant. For a given element, NCCL's summation order depends on where that element sits in the message (ring rotation, chunking, and the algorithm it picks for the message size). The training forward (`[s, b]` rows) and the inference engine (flat decode rows) place the same token at different positions, so they get different bits for that token. Measured on Ultra-L8 TP4xEP4 with the stock reduce: 576/576 tokens differed (max 1.3e-2). With the ordered reduce, all 576/576 were bitwise equal.

On HIP, every DeepSeek-V4.1 decode / target-verify metadata build ran small launches whose results V4.1 never reads, or that one existing launch can cover. With the mono kernels (`--monokernel-backend amd`), these launches are a visible share of a batch-1 DSpark step: about 15 of them go.

All in the HIP DeepSeek-V4 attention backend and its glue (`deepseek_v4_backend_hip_radix.py`, `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/attn_glue_hip.py`):

### Summary

For PaliGemma, `is_mm_prefix_lm` is True and the runner builds bidirectional ranges from `mm_features`, i.e. **the image placeholder span only**. PaliGemma's prefix is the image **and the instruction text after it** — its processor marks the whole prompt `token_type_id = 0`, and Transformers builds the bidirectional mask from that. Only the generated answer is causal.

The result is a mask that is bidirectional over the image but causal over the instruction, which is neither the HF contract nor fully causal.

items.title: [Bugfix][gRPC] Drain in-flight RPCs and engine work within --shutdown-timeout
items.author: mrn3088
items.summary: Fixes gRPC server ignoring --shutdown-timeout by draining in-flight RPCs and EngineCore work (e.g. NIXL block leases) within the configured budget instead of hardcoding 5s and SIGKILLing.
items.body:
## Overview

`vllm serve --grpc` ignores `--shutdown-timeout`. On SIGTERM it cancels in-flight RPCs after a hardcoded 5 s (`server.stop(grace=5.0)`). It then calls `AsyncLLM.shutdown()` without a timeout, so EngineCore gets the default 5 s join before SIGKILL. This PR spends the `--shutdown-timeout` budget in two phases: first the in-flight RPCs finish, then EngineCore drains work that outlives an RPC, such as NIXL prefill blocks that the decode side has not read yet.

items.title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Add speculator hooks for non-chain verification and draft suspension
items.author: seyfal
items.summary: This PR adds five optional hooks to Model Runner V2's, so a speculator can verify drafts that are not a chain (a tree, for example), choose how many drafts each request verifies, and stop drafting when speculation stops paying off at large batch sizes. Each ho…
items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds five optional hooks to Model Runner V2's `BaseSpeculator`, so a speculator can verify drafts that are not a chain (a tree, for example), choose how many drafts each request verifies, and stop drafting when speculation stops paying off at large batch sizes. Each hook defaults to today's behavior, and the runner calls a per-step hook only when the speculator overrides it, so built-in speculators run as before.

Model Runner V2 verifies drafts as a chain, and only built-in adaptive verification can change how many drafts a step verifies. A tree verifier needs to rewrite

items.title: [Spec Decode] Fix Dspark adaptive verification cost model
items.author: ekagra-ranjan
items.summary: Adaptive verification picks, every step, the draft budget that maximises The argmax depends only on how the slot price compares with the base. The current cost model gets both wrong, because it reads everything off a single profiled curve.
items.body:
## Summary

Adaptive verification picks, every step, the draft budget `b` that maximises

```
expected accepted tokens(b) / step cost(b)
step cost(b) = drafter cost + base + (price of b draft slots)
```

The argmax depends only on how the slot price compares with the base. The current cost model gets both wrong, because it reads everything off a single profiled curve. This PR profiles the two separately and prices the base from the batch's real shape and context.

items.summary: Optimizes DSpark speculative decoding by fusing the Markov walk into a single sm_90 kernel with int8 W2 quantization, reducing HBM traffic and achieving 3.7–7.7x speedup over eager per-step execution.
items.body:
## Overview

DSpark walks its draft block left to right: each step adds `W2 @ W1[prev]` to the base logits (W2 is V x 256) and then takes the argmax or a sample. Today every draft token is a full-vocab GEMV, an add and a sampler, and W2 (78 MB in bf16 at V = 151936) is read from HBM again on every step.

items.author: Waterpine

items.body:
## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. MegaMoE is the largest prefill cost in the BF16 TP8/EP8 deployment: about 68 ms of a 131 ms 8K-token TTFT on rank 0. For BF16 prefill shards DeepGEMM's heuristic picks BLOCK_M 192 (`2,192,48,128,2`), sized for uniformly spread routing. Muse Spark routing is skewed, and on GB300 `2,240,40,128,2` is faster for these shards. DeepGEMM reads `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES` on every MegaMoE launch; an empty value keeps its heuristic.

items.title: [Feat] tracing: Don't trace health checks
items.author: ryanguoRGBB
items.summary: and submit a one-token generation request (rid ), and the tokenizer traces it like any user request: root span, tokenizer and scheduler spans. With tracing on, every probe of every server adds a full trace, burying user requests in trace search and sampling.
items.body:
## Motivation

`/health` and `/health_generate` submit a one-token generation request (rid `HEALTH_CHECK_<uuid>`), and the tokenizer traces it like any user request: root span, tokenizer and scheduler spans. With tracing on, every probe of every server adds a full trace, burying user requests in trace search and sampling.

## Modifications

`init_trace_ctx` gives `HEALTH_CHECK_*` rids a null trace context, in both sync and async tracing, so health checks create no spans. `request_metrics_exporter` already skips these rids for the same reason (they are not user requests).

## Overview

With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a secondary-tier hit larger than the CPU tier loads nothing: the first KV cache group's promotions fill the CPU tier and every other group's promotions fail. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Hold promotions after a cache reset until jobs report
items.author: javieratomic
items.summary: Fixes a race condition in KV offloading where cache resets release CPU chunks before worker writes complete, causing incorrect KV data via secondary-tier promotions.
items.body:
## Overview

`reset_cache()` in the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler releases the CPU-tier chunks of in-flight transfer jobs at once, but the workers may still write those chunks until they report the jobs. With secondary tiers, a lookup in that window can promote a secondary-tier hit into one of the released chunks, and the late worker write then overwrites it, so a later load hands the GPU wrong KV. This PR holds promotions in the offloading manager after a cache reset until every worker has reported every flushed job.

It is a standalone bugfix on `main` and also applies to a single node.

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize beam search scores by generated length
items.author: 4arkeinlvy
items.summary: Fixes beam search score normalization to divide by generated length only (not prompt+generated), preventing early EOS bias and empty completions.
items.body:
## Overview

Beam search divides each beam's cumulative log-prob (a sum over the *generated* tokens) by `(prompt + generated length) ** length_penalty`. It should divide by the generated length only, as Transformers does. With any non-trivial prompt, the prompt length dominates the denominator, so `length_penalty` stops having an effect and beams that hit EOS early win, often with an empty completion. This affects `LLM.beam_search` and `use_beam_search` on `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and speech-to-text, which all share `create_sort_beams_key_function`.

## Motivation

`--preferred-sampling-params` is inert on `/v1/chat/completions`.

OpenAI defaults), so `obj.sampling_params` is always fully populated.
`TokenizerManager._create_tokenized_object` then merges
`{**preferred_sampling_params, **obj.sampling_params}`, and the request
dict always wins — the server-side row can never apply. With an empty
generation config, `top_k` additionally resolves to `-1`, silently
disabling top-k sampling

items.author: phambinhfin
items.summary: On gfx942 the GDN prefill kernels and never try the matrix instruction that is fastest on this hardware, because is absent from their autotune spaces. This appends gfx942-only configs behind; the kernel bodies are untouched and only the schedule changes.
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx942 the GDN prefill kernels `chunk_o` and `chunk_delta_h` never try the matrix instruction that is fastest on this hardware, because `matrix_instr_nonkdim` is absent from their autotune spaces. This appends gfx942-only configs behind `on_gfx942()`; the kernel bodies are untouched and only the schedule changes.

## Claims

- `chunk_o` is **1.83x** faster at the Qwen3-Next GDN prefill shape (1.0598 ms -> 0.5807 ms).
- `chunk_delta_h` is **1.12x** faster at the same shape (2.0857 ms -> 1.8648 ms).
- The single knob `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` is 53% of `chunk_o`'s recovered time

items.body:
## Overview

`NixlConnector` creates NIXL's UCX backend with `num_threads` only, so UCX runs with NIXL's default `ucx_error_handling_mode=peer`. In peer mode UCX wires up only transports that can detect peer failure. On one MI355X node that left tcp: GPU-to-GPU KV reads ran as software emulation over tcp at about 3.4 Gbps, while with `ucx_error_handling_mode=none` UCX picks rocm_ipc zero-copy and a 74 MiB read ran at 483.7 Gbps. `UCX_*` environment variables cannot set this (it is a NIXL backend init parameter), and vLLM has no way to pass one.

- New `kv_connector_extra_config.uc

items.title: [Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark: skip the draft forward on K=0 steps
items.author: jbelofamd
items.summary: A per-batch-size K schedule (, e.g. ) allows K=0 so that large batches run without speculation. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

A per-batch-size K schedule (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`, e.g. `[[1, 96, 7], [97, 2048, 0]]`) allows K=0 so that large batches run without speculation. The V2 runner passes that K to `propose()` and masks drafts past it, but `DFlashSpeculator.propose` (inherited by DSpark and DFlash2) ignores it, so every K=0 step still runs the full parallel draft forward and its sampling, and the runner throws the result away. Related: #47737 (open) fixes a ZeroDivisionError when a schedule containing 0 reaches DSpark's draft CUDA-graph capture; different file and bug, no code over

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Inkling: zero CUDA-graph padding rows in decode attention
items.author: jbelofamd
items.summary: Fixes GPU memory fault in ROCm Inkling decode attention by zeroing padding rows caused by CUDA-graph fixed-batch replay, preventing NaN propagation through MoE.
items.body:
## Overview

With `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs, Inkling on ROCm can hit a GPU memory fault in `fused_moe_kernel` once a few requests decode concurrently (`--enforce-eager` avoids it). Decode graphs are replayed at fixed batch sizes, so 3 live requests run in the batch-4 graph with one padding row. That row has `cache_seqlens` 0 and belongs to no request, but its attention output flows through the residual into the MoE gate, and two paths can leave NaN there. A NaN gate logit can make top-k return an index past the routed experts. Related: #61413 (open) moves this code to `inkling/common/`;

items.title: [Core] Route by exact in-flight count when a single client owns the DP engines
items.author: jbelofamd
items.summary: With one API server, routes by, where the second term is the coordinator's step-boundary snapshot. The snapshot lags the client's exact in-flight count, so the engine that just freed a slot ties with the full engines, and the rotating tie-break sends the repla…
items.body:
## Overview

With one API server, `DPLBAsyncMPClient` routes by `max(inflight, waiting + running)`, where the second term is the coordinator's step-boundary snapshot. The snapshot lags the client's exact in-flight count, so the engine that just freed a slot ties with the full engines, and the rotating tie-break sends the replacement to a full engine (DP-1)/DP of the time. Under closed-loop load one engine then runs one request over and one engine one under for a whole round, and lockstep DP+EP decode waits for the fuller one. items.title: [Fix] disagg: Do not gate PD decode radix prefix match on tree SWA
items.author: alphabetc1
items.summary: On a PD decode server with, decode matches the prompt against its tree but never reuses tree SWA. It caps the match at, releases the SWA lock, and allocates a fresh SWA tail that prefill always transfers.
items.body:
## Motivation

On a PD decode server with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`, decode matches the prompt against its tree but never reuses tree SWA. It caps the match at `fill - swa_tail_len`, releases the SWA lock, and allocates a fresh SWA tail that prefill always transfers. Paged SWA still gates that match, though. A boundary counts only if a full window of live tree SWA sits before it. Decode evicts SWA behind its window while decoding, so a match capped in the middle of a node finds no live window and falls back to 0.

items.title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek-V4.1] Honor continue_final_message: render the last assistant turn without EOS
items.author: reyanshsolis
items.summary: Fixes DeepSeek-V4.1 tokenizer to respect continue_final_message flag, preventing unwanted EOS token from closing the final assistant turn.
items.body:
## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4.1 tokenizer (`--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41`) ignores `continue_final_message`. A request that asks the model to continue an assistant prefix ("prefill") is rendered with a closed assistant turn: the prefix ends with `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>`, so the model is asked to continue after EOS. This makes the last assistant message `wo_eos` when `continue_final_message` is set, which is what DeepSeek's reference encoder does.

Related: #43876 fixes the same gap for the **V4** tokenizer (`vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py`); this PR is the **V4.1** tokenizer (`vllm/tokenizers/dee

items.title: [CPU][Zen] Give the int8 MoE experts slack for the in-place reorder
items.author: ganeshr10
items.summary: Adds per-expert padding to enable in-place weight reordering for ZenDNN int8 MoE, cutting peak memory by ~20 GiB versus the previous duplicate-all-experts fallback.
items.body:
ZenDNN reorders int8 MoE expert weights in place only when each expert has room for the `N * 4` byte compensation row that follows it. `process_weights_after_loading` leaves them packed back-to-back, so it falls back to duplicating every expert instead.

zentorch exposes the fix as an op, `zentorch_preprocess_weights` which re-allocates an `[E, N, K]` int8 weight with slack after each expert.
The call fires only when `experts_cls is ZenCPUExpertsInt8` **and** zentorch has the op registered. Every other quantization path, backend and platform is byte-identical.

## Validation

Unit coverage add

items.author: BugenZhao
items.summary: A structured-output constraint that EngineCore fails to compile finishes the request as with no error attached. The Python frontend rarely sees this, because it validates constraints with the backend library before submitting.
items.body:
## Overview

A structured-output constraint that EngineCore fails to compile finishes the request as `FINISHED_ERROR` with no error attached. The Python frontend rarely sees this, because it validates constraints with the backend library before submitting. The Rust frontend cannot, so its clients get HTTP 500 for an invalid regex or grammar, and an empty 200 when llguidance builds a matcher in an error state (for example a schema with `uniqueItems`). This PR reports compile failures with the `validation_error` code that #49625 introduced for backend mismatches, so both frontends return 400,

## Description

Fixes #20745.

`DSparkSpecMetadata.prepare()` resets the scratch row of the embedded DSpark worker on every iteration with `cuda_tensor[i] = <python scalar>`. All the host work between that point and the next graph launch then becomes GPU idle time.

items.title: fix: run dense fused kernels through the FSDP2 LM head
items.author: ZiyiXu06
items.summary: Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads, including models such as Qwen3. Previously, the fused forward accessed directly, bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular Tensors with DTensors during matrix multipl…
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.summary: scans all of a request's other cached inputs on every call, so freeing a request with N multimodal items is O(N²) on the scheduler thread. This makes it O(N) with the same release semantics.
items.body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #54284. `EncoderCacheManager.free_encoder_input` scans all of a request's other cached inputs on every call, so freeing a request with N multimodal items is O(N²) on the scheduler thread. This makes it O(N) with the same release semantics.

## Claims

- Freeing a request with N multimodal items is now linear in N: 1,024 items drops from 15.9 ms to 0.29 ms, and 4,096 from 235 ms to 1.2 ms.
- No behaviour change: an entry is still held until the request's last occurrence of that `mm_hash` is freed, as #54284 requires.
- Only matters for prompts with hundreds of items

items.title: [Fix] sampling: Add upper bounds for top_k, top_logprobs_num and n
items.author: zichen0116
items.summary: All checks are inline at the point where the value is consumed; no new helpers. The sentinel (the post- form of, and also the default) stays exempt, so whole-vocabulary sampling is unaffected.
items.body:
Fixes #41482.

`SamplingParams.verify()` range-checks almost every field, but `top_k`, `top_logprobs_num` and `n` had no upper bound. A single request with `top_k=2147483648` overflows int32 in the scheduler event loop and takes the whole server down (SIGQUIT, all in-flight requests lost), while a huge `n` fans one prompt out into an unbounded number of copies during request normalization. Out-of-range values for the other fields are rejected cleanly with `ValueError`; these three slipped through.

### Changes

All checks are inline at the point where the value is consumed; no new helpers.

items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Avoid re-marking committed prompt-tail boundaries as cached this step
items.author: khyun1109
items.summary: Fixes Mamba cache manager re-caching already-committed prompt-tail boundaries, enabling fan-out requests over shared prefixes to be admitted together instead of one per step.
items.body:
## Overview

On hybrid models with `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (e.g. Qwen3.5), requests whose prompts share their last hash-aligned boundary are admitted one per engine step once that boundary is committed. This hits reads fanned out over one prompt and the children of a parallel-sampling request (`n > 1`). This PR skips re-caching that boundary in `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` when the block already carries its hash, so these requests are admitted together. Related: #29387 (the same-step guard this interacts with), #61192 (`/v1/systemone` reads over one state, which take this path).

items.author: panpan0000

## Purpose

Add a fused TileLang kernel for the **DSpark confidence head** used by adaptive speculative decoding. The shape:

```
p_accept = sigmoid( ( [hidden_state ; markov_embed] @ W ) / temperature )

items.title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Replay one row for prefill chunks far from the prompt end
items.author: ischencheng
items.summary: With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end.
items.body:
## Overview

With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end. A 124K prompt in 16K chunks now skips 7 of its 8 replay tails. The same idea is DeepSeek DeepInfer's `clip_prefix` rule.

Related: #61682 does this on ROCm with one row for every unfinished chunk. That rule lets a later step read replay-layer KV that no step wrote (inline comment there). This PR covers CUDA and keeps that case closed

items.author: yashaswikarnati
items.summary: Packed MTP currently exchanges CP boundary tokens once per document. This change batches all documents into one boundary vector per neighbor per roll, and vectorizes local packed rolls and HSM boundary translation.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

Packed MTP currently exchanges CP boundary tokens once per document. This change batches all documents into one boundary vector per neighbor per roll, and vectorizes local packed rolls and HSM boundary translation.

With zigzag CP > 1, physical document lengths must be divisible by `2 * cp_size`; invalid lengths raise `ValueError`. Slots after the final document roll as a separate segment, ending in zero.

# What does this PR do?

Batch-invariant (BI) inference with MXFP8 routed experts does work proportional to `max_tokens` on every decode step, whatever the number of live tokens. This PR bounds that work by the live rows, which the kernels already read on device. CUDA graphs keep their static shapes, and the quantized and reduced rows are bitwise unchanged.

items.body:
## Description

`MiniMaxM3Gate` computes its router logits in FP32 with `F.linear(hidden_states.float(), weight)`. That has two costs. `F.linear` follows torch's FP32 matmul precision, which the NGC PyTorch containers set to TF32 through `TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE=1`; at TF32 the logits move enough to flip near-tied top-4 expert choices against the FP32 reference (SGLang routes this model in FP32). And a true FP32 GEMM cannot use tensor cores, so this small per-layer op runs as a SIMT SGEMM.

This change keeps FP32-grade routing on tensor cores:

- `load_weights` splits the FP32 router

## 1. Summary

In GRPO-style RL in verl every prompt is sampled `rollout.n` times, so the actor, reference and critic each run a forward pass over every (prompt, response) pair and process the same prompt `n` times per group. items.title: [None][perf] MiniMax-M3: split decode index scoring across TP ranks
items.author: zheyuf
items.summary: To do that, it reads the whole index-K cache: one 128-dim FP8 key per cached token, in each of the 57 sparse layers. Every TP rank reads all of index-K to score only its own index heads, so the same bytes are read TP times.
items.body:
## Description

**Problem.** In each MiniMax-M3 decode step, the index scorer picks the 16 KV blocks every query attends to. To do that, it reads the whole index-K cache: one 128-dim FP8 key per cached token, in each of the 57 sparse layers. Every TP rank reads all of index-K to score only its own index heads, so the same bytes are read TP times. At 131k-token contexts this read dominates the scorer: about 70 µs per layer at TP2, batch 24.

**What this PR does** (`sparse_attention_config.index_tp_split`, off by default):
- **Split the read.** Rank r reads rows r, r + TP, ... of every 128-token

items.author: pranav-nvidia
items.summary: With TP spanning nodes the AUTO all-reduce strategy selects the MNNVL all-reduce, and a model compiled with fails in warmup on every rank with. Two things on that path cannot be compiled. [Discussion: @coderabbitai full review]
items.body:
## Description

With TP spanning nodes the AUTO all-reduce strategy selects the MNNVL all-reduce, and a model compiled with `enable_fullgraph: true` fails in warmup on every rank with `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: call to a callable object with no traceable __call__`. Two things on that path cannot be compiled. The cached-workspace lookup in `get_or_scale_allreduce_mnnvl_workspace` calls `is_mapped()` on the nanobind workspace handle and then `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, neither of which Dynamo can trace. Behind that, functionalization rejects `trtllm::mnnvl_fusion_allreduce`

items.body:
## Description

# What does this PR do?

With batch-invariant inference and MLA latent caching enabled, a new request entering prefill can change the generated log-probabilities of requests already decoding. Use unabsorbed attention for both paths when `batch_invariant_mode=True`, as required by the [batch-invariant inference guarantee](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ce852bfb93f3

Unit tests in CI have intermittent hangs, most notably in the GDN unit tests, but also in other test suites more rarely.

items.title: fix(inference): promote TorchSampling temperature divisor to FP32
items.author: muditagrawal2007
items.summary: ran in the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that - loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and - overflows FP16 at temperature=0 (the divisor is floored to → → ).
items.body:
Fixes #7857.

## What

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` ran `last_token_logits.div_(temperature)` in
the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that

  - loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership
    at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and
  - overflows FP16 at temperature=0 (the divisor is floored to
    `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6` → `logits * 1e6` → `inf`).

Issue #7857 documents both failures on a trained Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K through
the dynamic engine: BF16 rounding changes which token wins at temperature=0.1,
top_p=0.9; FP16 scaling overflows at temperature=0.

`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

```python
PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

# What does this PR do?

items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout.
items.body:
**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688) in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1

### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.title: [reward] fix: handle dict-returning score functions in PrimeRewardManager
items.author: Virtuoso461
items.summary: Fixes #8216 ### What does this PR do? in had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (mathdapo, rlla,...) hit, raised, and 's except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.
items.body:
Fixes #8216

### What does this PR do?

`parallel_compute_score_async` in `PrimeRewardManager` had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (math_dapo, rlla, ...) hit `float(result[0])`, raised `KeyError: 0`, and `verify()`'s except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.

This adds the same `isinstance(result, dict) -> result["score"]` handling that `NaiveRewardManager` / `BatchRewardManager` / `DAPORewardManager` already have.

### Tests

New `tests/workers/reward_manager/test_prime_on_cpu.py` (CPU-only):
- dict result -> uses "score" key (failed before this fix)

items.author: Virtuoso461

items.body:
### Describe the bug

`PrimeRewardManager` (`verl/workers/reward_manager/prime.py`) crashes the result-processing loop of `parallel_compute_score_async` with `KeyError: 0` whenever the reward function returns a dict such as `{"score": 1.0, "acc": True, "pred": "42"}` — which is exactly what `math_dapo.compute_score`, `rlla.compute_score` and several custom reward functions return (`default_compute_score` passes dicts through unchanged).

The KeyError is then swallowed by `PrimeRewardManager.verify`'s `except Exception` fallback, so **the entire batch gets reward 0.0** with only a single print

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. A `BaseTool` therefore cannot keep state from one turn to the next, although `BaseTool.create` is documented as creating "a tool instance for a trajectory" and `docs/sglang_multiturn/multiturn.rst` points to `BaseTool` for per-trajectory state such as sandbox VMs, scratch directories and DB rows.

This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

- DeepScaler

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Each model rank reports the next rollout ID after loading, while rollout data is restored from the preceding completed rollout. In mode, later actor recreations discarded their returned checkpoint IDs.
items.body:
## Background

Slime resumes PPO training from actor, optional critic, and rollout-data checkpoints. Each model rank reports the next rollout ID after loading, while rollout data is restored from the preceding completed rollout.

## Problem

The startup path previously selected one set of returned IDs without checking that:

- all actor ranks loaded the same rollout
- all critic ranks loaded the same rollout
- actor and critic checkpoints agree
- an explicit `--start-rollout-id` matches the loaded model state

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

Fixes #2268

## Problem

`slime/utils/reloadable_process_group.py::_wrap_low_level_call` runs a memory probe **before every wrapped collective**:

```python
def _wrap_low_level_call(check_memory=True):
    if check_memory:

        if mem_info["free_GB"] < 3:
            clear_memory()
    yield
```

## 1. Background

VIME can already load an external EAGLE/DFlash/Dspark.. Draft model through vLLM's `SpeculativeConfig` for speculative decoding. This lowers Draft-token acceptance and average acceptance length, and may
eventually make the additional Draft and verification cost larger than the speculative-decoding benefit.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.
